title: The Collier in the Red Cap: Philipp Griebel, the Thuringian Forest, and the Object That Outran Its Maker
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Ilmenau, the mines reopened
stops.date_confidence: attested for Goethe; pin inherited byte-identical from goethe_full.journey.json. The link to Griebel's clay is inferred [R].
stops.campa: Ten kilometres from Gräfenroda, in the same fold of the Thuringian Forest, Goethe takes charge of the silver and copper workings at Ilmenau for the Duke of Weimar and spends years learning the rock by hand, hiring engineers, measuring shafts, writing reports on drainage. He sets the Wandrers Nachtlied on the wall of the Gickelhahn hut above the pits. The geology he surveys as a mining administrator is the geology that puts clay under Gräfenroda, and the colliers he counts underground are the men whose bearded, hooded, lantern-carrying likeness a village modeller will fire in terracotta a century later.
suggested_refs: The Ilmenau mining administration papers, 1776-1796
The Gickelhahn hut above Ilmenau
sources: de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gartenzwerg (Thuringian mining folklore behind the figure)

stops.name: Oberweissbach, the parsonage in the same forest
stops.date_confidence: attested for Fröbel; pin inherited byte-identical from froebel.journey.json. The proximity argument is inferred [R].
stops.campa: Friedrich Fröbel is born in the parsonage of Oberweissbach, along the ridge from Gräfenroda in the principality of Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt. He will give the German language the word Kindergarten and the world its first one, at Bad Blankenburg in 1837. The same small forest district, the same patchwork of tiny courts and craft villages, sends two objects of childhood out to the rest of the world within a hundred years: the kindergarten, and the garden gnome. No source connects them. The geography does, and the geography is about forty kilometres wide.
suggested_refs: Oberweissbach parish church
Bad Blankenburg, the first Kindergarten, 1837

stops.name: Aussig an der Elbe, the Siderolith works
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: the 1841 founding is given by steinmarks.co.uk and moaph.org and could not be confirmed against any live primary source.
stops.campa: Adolf Baehr and Johann Maresch open a terracotta works at the corner of Teplitzerstrasse and Johannesstrasse in Aussig on the Elbe and make what the trade calls Siderolith: hard, painted, weatherproof earthenware figures for gardens. Under Ferdinand Maresch the firm will export across Europe and to the United States, stop production in 1944 and close in 1948. Popular garden history habitually moves the factory to Dresden. The address does not move. Whatever the first garden gnome was, figures of this kind were leaving this yard before Philipp Griebel had a workshop.
suggested_refs: Baehr & Maresch factory marks, Aussig an der Elbe
Museum of Applied Arts and Sciences, Maresch holdings
sources: moaph.org, 'Exploring the Legacy of Johann and Ferdinand Maresch'

stops.name: Nuremberg, the terracottas an English baronet buys
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Nuremberg attribution (de.wikipedia, Gartenzwerg); pin inherited byte-identical from savitri_devi.journey.json.
stops.campa: German Wikipedia says plainly where Sir Charles Isham's figures came from: 'Sir Charles Isham besaß Terrakottafiguren aus Nürnberg und nutzte sie als Bereicherung des Steingartens von Lamport Hall.' Nuremberg, not Gräfenroda. The English literature will spend a century and a half saying otherwise, crediting a Thuringian workshop that does not yet exist to a man who may not yet be born. A crate of little clay men crosses the Channel from that same Nuremberg trade, proof the shape was already moving through commerce before any single village could claim to have invented it.
stops.quote: Sir Charles Isham besaß Terrakottafiguren aus Nürnberg und nutzte sie als Bereicherung des Steingartens von Lamport Hall.
suggested_refs: Nuremberg terracotta and toy trade of the 1840s

stops.name: Lamport Hall, twenty-one gnomes in the rockery
stops.date_confidence: attested for the event; the attribution to Griebel is contradicted and is carried as legend [R]. Coordinates corrected to Wikidata Q6482482.
stops.campa: Isham builds a rock garden of clinker and stone at Lamport Hall in Northamptonshire and populates it with twenty-one terracotta figures brought from Germany, working the miniature landscape the way a spiritualist works a table, a small world with small inhabitants. English Wikipedia states they were 'manufactured in Germany by Philip Griebel'. Griebel founds his firm in 1874 and dies in 1893. The arithmetic refuses. German Wikipedia introduces the same year with 'erneut', again: 1847 is not even the first English mention of the figures.
stops.quote: In 1847, Sir Charles Isham, brought 21 terracotta gnomes manufactured in Germany by Philip Griebel back to Britain
suggested_refs: The Lamport Hall rockery and its surviving gnome
Sir Charles Isham, 10th Baronet, spiritualist and rock gardener

stops.name: Rudolstadt, the assembly in the year of revolutions
stops.date_confidence: attested for the assembly; pin inherited byte-identical from froebel.journey.json. The Griebel backdrop is inferred [R].
stops.campa: In the revolutionary summer the German teachers gather at Rudolstadt and argue Fröbel's kindergarten cause in the seat of the principality that also contains Gräfenroda. Small-court Thuringia is coming apart and rearranging itself: dozens of duchies and principalities, each with its own tariffs and roads and its own export trade in toys, glass, porcelain and clay. Somewhere in this district a boy is growing up who will fire the region's most exported object. No source records where he is, or how old.
suggested_refs: Rudolstadt, Heidecksburg above the town
1848 teachers' assembly proceedings

segments.name: Gräfenroda, a Man Without a Birth Date

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the missing birth
stops.date_confidence: unattested. No source gives Philipp Griebel's birth year or birthplace; the date shown is a placeholder inferred backward from the 1860 apprenticeship and carries no authority.
stops.campa: German Wikipedia, English Wikipedia and the manufactory's own history page were each fetched, and each gives the same thing for Philipp Griebel's birth: nothing. No year, no village, no parents, no parish. His death in 1893 is recorded; the other end of the life is open. This is the first fact about him and it governs all the rest, because the claim most often made about him in English, that he supplied Isham's gnomes in 1847, cannot even be tested against an age. He arrives in the record already a journeyman.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda parish registers, not consulted and not known to be digitised

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the porcelain apprenticeship completed
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page; single-source and self-reported. German Wikipedia confirms the trade and gives no year.
stops.campa: He finishes his apprenticeship as a Porzelliner, a porcelain maker. The date comes from the firm's own history page and appears in no independent source. The research pool behind this journey carried 1860 as a contradiction against a second date of 1874, taking the two for rival accounts of one training. They are not rivals. They are two trainings on one page, in order, and the conflict was manufactured in transmission rather than found in the sources. Thuringian porcelain is an industry by 1860; a village boy learns it the way another learns joinery.
stops.quote: His founder, Philipp Griebel, completed his apprenticeship as a 'porcelain maker' in 1860.
suggested_refs: Thuringian porcelain apprenticeship records, 1850s-1860s

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Heinrich Dornheim's animal heads
stops.date_confidence: inferred [R]. The source places this training after 1860 and before 1874 and dates it nowhere; the year shown is a placeholder inside that span.
stops.campa: He goes on to learn a second trade under the animal-head manufacturer Heinrich Dornheim of Gräfenroda: Tierkopfmodelleur, modeller of animal heads, the stags and boars and hounds that hang on hunting-lodge walls across the German lands. Dornheim's name survives on the manufactory's page and nowhere else; German Wikipedia records the trade and not the master. What the second apprenticeship gives him is the thing the gnome will require, a hand for faces that are not quite human faces and are not meant to be.
suggested_refs: Heinrich Dornheim, Tierkopffabrikant, Gräfenroda: no independent record located

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the commendatory certificate
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page; single-source, self-reported, and no archive is named as holding the document.
stops.campa: Dornheim releases him with a commendatory certificate, the trade's formal statement that the work is good. Only the firm says so. It is the last document of his apprenticeship and the only piece of paper about Philipp Griebel that anyone claims to have seen, and no reachable source reproduces it or names a repository that holds it. The certificate stands as the house's own telling of its founding, and nothing more. Everything he does after this point is done as a master.
suggested_refs: The commendatory certificate of 1874, cited by the manufactory, location unstated

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the Thonwarenfabrik founded
stops.date_confidence: attested; the one date in the biography given independently by more than one source.
stops.campa: In the same year he opens his own terracotta works in the village. This is the single date in the whole biography that two independent sources supply: German Wikipedia states it twice, and the manufactory repeats it. Gräfenroda has clay, kilns and a ceramics habit already, and August Heissner has started a rival works two years earlier. What Griebel makes at first is animals, garden ware and the ordinary output of a Thuringian Thonwarenfabrik. The figure the village will be known for is six years off, and will not be his alone.
stops.quote: Philipp Griebel, der Ausbildungen als Porzelliner und Tierkopfmodelleur absolviert hatte, gründete 1874 das Unternehmen.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda trade register entries, 1874
August Heissner works, Gräfenroda, founded 1872

segments.name: The Fair, and the Figure Takes Shape

stops.name: Leipzig, animal figures at the trade fair
stops.date_confidence: inferred [R]. The source says 'only two years later' and prints no year; 1876 is that count made explicit.
stops.campa: The workshop shows its animal figures at the Leipzig fair, the clearing house through which Thuringian craft reaches the world. The manufactory's page dates the appearance by counting rather than by year: only two years after the founding. Leipzig will matter twice more in this story, once in a claim that cannot be checked because its source has gone off the web, and once in a plain sentence of German Wikipedia that puts the gnome's arrival at this fair twenty-two years later than the firm's own chronology would like.
suggested_refs: Leipzig Messe exhibitor catalogues, 1870s

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the two sons
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page only. The research pool's attribution of these lifespans to English Wikipedia is false, verified by direct fetch: that article names neither brother.
stops.campa: August Griebel is born in 1877, Wendelin in 1884. Both dates, and the deaths in 1954 and 1945, come from the firm's history page and from nowhere else. These two will carry the whole weight of the succession problem, because German Wikipedia has Wendelin running the company from 1893, and a boy born in 1884 is nine years old in 1893. Nothing in the reachable record resolves it, and the conflict is not between Wikipedia and a hobby site; it is between Wikipedia and the family's own account of itself.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda civil registers for the Griebel family, not located

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the gnomes begin
stops.date_confidence: decade only. The source reads 'Ab den 1880er Jahren'; the single year is a placeholder, and the pool's rendering of it as the year 1880 has been marked as such.
stops.campa: From the 1880s onward he makes garden gnomes. That one clause is the entire sentence German Wikipedia devotes to the turn on which everything else rests. The manufactory's page enlarges it: between 1880 and 1890 Griebel works the figure out alongside several other Gräfenroda modellers, collectively, a village solving a form rather than a man inventing one. Which of them did what is not recorded anywhere, and the firm that carries his name has never claimed the invention for him.
stops.quote: Ab den 1880er Jahren produzierte er Gartenzwerge.
suggested_refs: Surviving Gräfenroda terracotta gnome moulds of the 1880s

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the red cap
stops.date_confidence: tradition [R]: the house's own account, seen via search summary of the manufactory's 'The Gnome' page rather than direct fetch. The year is a placeholder inside the 1880-1890 span.
stops.campa: The house tradition explains the figure item by item. The red cap is a miner's cap, padded to take falling stone off the neck and shoulders. The clothes are working clothes. The lantern is a pit lantern, and the wheelbarrow and the basket are what a man moves ore in. The Thuringian Forest is silver and copper country, and the small bearded man standing in a flowerbed is a collier at the surface. This is the manufactory explaining its own product, which does not make it false and does not make it evidence.
suggested_refs: Zwergstatt Gräfenroda, 'The Gnome' page: not fetched directly, search summary only

stops.name: Weimar, the archive forty-five kilometres off
stops.date_confidence: attested for Steiner; pin inherited byte-identical from steiner.journey.json. The contemporaneity argument with Griebel is inferred [R].
stops.campa: Rudolf Steiner spends seven years in Weimar editing Goethe's scientific manuscripts in the Goethe-Schiller Archive, forty-five kilometres down the road from Gräfenroda, in exactly the years the village is turning its collier figure into an export article. The duchy that keeps the archive and the village that fires the gnomes are the same small state. High culture and folk craft are being catalogued and crated out of one forest in one decade, and neither party sets down a word about the other.
suggested_refs: Goethe-Schiller-Archiv, Weimar, Steiner's editorial years 1890-1896

segments.name: The Death, and What the Object Did Next

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Philipp Griebel dies
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year only; no month, no day, and no burial place is given in any reachable source.
stops.campa: He dies in 1893, aged nobody knows what. No source located gives a burial place, a cemetery, a stone, or a date inside the year. There is no will in evidence, no inventory of the works, no obituary reproduced anywhere. What survives him is a firm that will keep his name for another hundred and thirty years and a village that will be identified ever after with a single object. The figure itself his own descendants describe as the work of several hands. Where his grave should be there is a hole in the record that nothing has filled.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda cemetery: no Griebel grave identified in any reachable source

stops.name: Naumburg, the archive of another Thuringian name
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Nietzsche-Archiv; pin inherited byte-identical from nietzsche.journey.json. The parallel with Griebel is inferred [R].
stops.campa: The year after Griebel's death, Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche founds the Nietzsche-Archiv in the house at Weingarten 18 in Naumburg, where her brother lies mute upstairs, and begins the manufacture of a philosopher. Sixty kilometres southwest the Griebel works is manufacturing a Volk figure of another kind. Both are late-century German industries in the making of a national type, one in edited manuscripts and one in fired clay, and only one of the two knows that this is what it is doing.
suggested_refs: Nietzsche-Haus, Weingarten 18, Naumburg, and the founding of the Nietzsche-Archiv, 1894

stops.name: Leipzig, offered as Thuringian for the first time
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'erstmals' in de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gartenzwerg. Contradicts both the firm's 1876 count and an unverifiable 1884 date.
stops.campa: In 1898 Thuringian gnomes are offered at the Leipzig fair for the first time. The sentence is flat and it wrecks two other dates: the firm's own count that puts Griebel at Leipzig in 1876, which was animals and not gnomes, and a widely repeated 1884 breakthrough whose only source, das-ist-thueringen.de, now returns a 404 at every URL tried. The gnome becomes a regional brand five years after the death of the man the region credits with it. Three dates for one arrival, and no way to reconcile them.
stops.quote: 1898 wurden Thüringer Zwerge erstmals auf der Leipziger Messe angeboten.
suggested_refs: Leipzig Messe catalogues, 1898
das-ist-thueringen.de, 'Der Gartenzwerg': HTTP 404, unreachable

stops.name: Lamport Hall, the daughters and the survivor
stops.date_confidence: attested; Isham died in 1903 and the clearance of the rockery followed his death.
stops.campa: Isham dies and his daughters, who never cared for the little men in the rockery, have them cleared out and destroyed. One is missed, wedged in a crevice, and is found again long afterward. He is called Lampy, he is kept inside the house rather than in the garden, and English Wikipedia records that he is insured for one million pounds: the oldest surviving garden gnome in the world, and the last physical object connecting the English tradition to a German kiln that nobody can now name with confidence.
stops.quote: Nicknamed 'Lampy', the only gnome of the original batch to survive is on display at Lamport Hall and insured for £1 million.
suggested_refs: Lampy, on display at Lamport Hall, Northamptonshire

stops.name: Royal Hospital Chelsea, the gnome forbidden
stops.date_confidence: attested; consistently reported across NBC, ITV and GB News coverage. The pool's '1920s' is wrong by a decade, and 1912 is what makes 2013 reportable as the end of a hundred-year ban.
stops.campa: The Royal Horticultural Society moves its great show to the grounds of the Royal Hospital Chelsea and rules, in the same year, that garden gnomes have no place in it. Brightly coloured mythical creatures are struck from the list of things a serious garden may contain. The ban will hold for a century. Nineteen years after the death of the man the trade credits with him, the collier in the red cap is a figure the Royal Horticultural Society names in writing in order to keep him out.
suggested_refs: RHS Chelsea Flower Show rules on 'brightly coloured mythical creatures'
sources: NBC News, 'Banned garden gnomes make triumphant return to Chelsea Flower Show'
ITV coverage of the 2013 centenary show

stops.name: Gräfenroda, August and Wendelin after the First War
stops.date_confidence: inferred [R]. The source gives no year, only 'after the First World War'; the pool's 1919 is not in it.
stops.campa: Of the Gräfenroda manufacturers some fifteen come through the war still working, the Griebel terracotta factory among them, run now by the two brothers. The research pool moved that figure to the aftermath of the Second World War; the manufactory's page puts it after the First, and the correction matters because it is the difference between a trade thinned and a trade wiped out. In England the same years run the other way. Gardeners smash German-made gnomes for being German-made, and the works that supplied them have been turned to war production.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda terracotta trade after 1918
sources: mentalfloss.com, 'A Brief History of Garden Gnomes' (aggregate, [R])

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Willi Griebel born
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page only (1920-2000). English Wikipedia, cited for it in the pool, carries nothing about Willi Griebel.
stops.campa: Willi Griebel is born, grandson of Philipp. He will run the firm through the Nazi years, through the 1948 ban, through the whole of the German Democratic Republic, and will still be at the bench of what was once his own property when the state has owned it for eight years. His dates come from the family firm and from no independent record, and English Wikipedia, cited for them in the research pool, carries nothing about him at all. Three generations of Griebels are documented entirely by the fourth generation's website.
suggested_refs: Willi Griebel, 1920-2000, per the manufactory's history page

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Wendelin hands over
stops.date_confidence: decade only: 'In den 1930er Jahren' (de.wikipedia). The pool's 1935 is invented precision and has been removed.
stops.campa: Some time in the 1930s Wendelin gives the leadership of the works to his son Willi. German Wikipedia gives the decade and refuses the year; the research pool supplied 1935, which no source contains, and it has been taken back out. This is the third of five places where a decade in a German sentence became a single confident year somewhere in transmission. The pattern matters more than any one of the dates does: a thin record attracts a precision it cannot support, and then keeps it.
stops.quote: In den 1930er Jahren übergab Wendelin die Führung an seinen Sohn Willi.
suggested_refs: Gartenzwergmanufaktur Philipp Griebel, management succession records: none located

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the year of the seven dwarfs
stops.date_confidence: attested for the effect (en.wikipedia, Garden gnome). The placement at Gräfenroda is editorial: the source gives no location, and the claim is about Western markets at large.
stops.campa: Disney releases Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, and the garden gnome stops being a German curiosity and becomes a mass article. English Wikipedia credits the film with the surge in popularity and in cheapness that carries the figure across class lines in Western markets. The Gräfenroda collier, modelled on the men who worked the Thuringian pits, is absorbed into an American cartoon of the same men and comes back out the other side selling in numbers no trade fair had ever produced for it.
suggested_refs: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, 1937, and the interwar gnome market

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the kilns through the war
stops.date_confidence: attested by implication only: German Wikipedia says the first interruption came in 1948. The pool's 1943 anchor is invented; English Wikipedia says the opposite for the industry at large.
stops.campa: German Wikipedia says Griebel production was interrupted for the first time only in 1948, which means the kilns burned through the war. English Wikipedia says the opposite about the trade as a whole: the war and the years after it saw a decline in the industry and caused most producers to halt manufacture. Both cannot be describing the same shed. Neither source addresses the other, and this journey does not adjudicate; it records that a garden ornament was still being fired somewhere in Thuringia in the middle of it.
stops.quote: World War II and the years following saw a decline in the industry, causing most producers to halt their manufacture.
suggested_refs: Wartime ceramics allocation in Thuringia, 1939-1945: no record located

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Wendelin dies
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page only; the pool's citation of English Wikipedia for this date is false.
stops.campa: Wendelin Griebel dies as the war ends, sixty-one years old if the firm's dates are right, fifty-two years after German Wikipedia says he took charge of the company at the age of nine. He is the pivot of the contradiction and he leaves it standing. His brother August will outlive him by nine years and appears in no account of the firm after this point. The works passes on, or has already passed on, to Willi, in a decade nobody dated, under a state that is about to change twice inside four years.
suggested_refs: Wendelin Griebel, 1884-1945, per the manufactory's history page

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Thuringia forbids garden figures
stops.date_confidence: attested. The pool's cited source (thueringen-lese.de) returns 404 and its caution flag has been dropped: German Wikipedia states this directly.
stops.campa: The Land of Thuringia bans the manufacture of garden figures and the Griebel kilns go out for the first time in seventy-four years. A softer version of the episode circulates in tourism copy, in which the ministry merely finds gnomes unnecessary under socialism before permitting them again for hard-currency export; that version could not be verified on any live page, and is kept beside the ban rather than merged into it. The ban itself is in German Wikipedia, one sentence, without qualification.
stops.quote: Erst 1948 musste die Produktion vorübergehend unterbrochen werden, als das Land Thüringen die Herstellung von Gartenfiguren verbot.
suggested_refs: Land Thüringen decree on garden figures, 1948: text not located

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Reinhard Griebel born
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page.
stops.campa: Reinhard Griebel is born, great-grandson of Philipp. He will be thirty-seven when the state that owns his family's workshop ceases to exist, and he will take the name back in the same year. Between his birth and that year the firm will be enlarged, absorbed, and renamed under two different state enterprises depending on which source is telling it, and emptied of the last Griebel to work in it. He is the fourth generation and the last of the name to run the works, and the first about whom the record is complete: a birth year, a career, a retirement date. His great-grandfather has none of those.
suggested_refs: Reinhard Griebel, born 1953, fourth generation

stops.name: Gräfenroda, new works and twenty hands
stops.date_confidence: decade only: 'In den 1960er Jahren' (de.wikipedia). The pool's 1962 is invented precision.
stops.campa: New production buildings go up in the 1960s and the manufactory employs about twenty people. Twenty is the only firm headcount in any reliable source. A claim of more than fifty employees under Willi before nationalization circulates and entered the research pool as attested to the firm's own page; it is not on that page, and it sits badly against German Wikipedia's twenty. Both numbers are recorded here and neither is adopted, because nothing available decides between them.
stops.quote: In den 1960er Jahren wurden neue Betriebsstätten errichtet, die Gartenzwergmanufaktur beschäftigte damals etwa 20 Mitarbeiter.
suggested_refs: Gräfenroda works buildings of the 1960s

stops.name: Gräfenroda, expropriated under two different names
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the name of the successor state enterprise is contradicted between the two best sources and is left open.
stops.campa: The East German state completes the expropriation. German Wikipedia describes a nationalization in two phases, finished in 1972, merging the works with the firm Balzer & Bock into VEB Terrakotta. The manufactory's own page describes the works being folded into the state combine VEB Gräfenroda-Keramik. Two names for one event, from the two best sources there are. The research pool presented the second as settled fact and added a street address that appears nowhere; the address is dropped and the contradiction restored.
suggested_refs: VEB Terrakotta and VEB Gräfenroda-Keramik: company registers not consulted

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the gnome as currency
stops.date_confidence: tradition [R]: search summaries of tourism copy, not verified against a live page. The year is a placeholder inside the 1970s-1980s span.
stops.campa: Inside the GDR the garden gnome becomes a scarce good and therefore a soft currency. It is traded for a holiday booking, for roof tiles, for a plumber's afternoon, in an economy where the thing you can actually get is worth more than the money you hold. The same object leaves through the export gate for West German marks. A state with no ideological use for a bearded collier in a red cap discovers that it has an unusually reliable one on its hands.
suggested_refs: GDR informal exchange and consumer scarcity, 1970s-1980s

stops.name: West Putford, four acres of them
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, Gnome Reserve). The Gnome Club of Great Britain and its 1978 date are not in that article and are carried separately as [R]. Coordinates corrected from the pool.
stops.campa: Ann Atkin founds the Gnome Reserve in a Devon combe: four acres of woodland and wildflower meadow given over to more than two thousand gnomes and pixies, with pointed hats issued at the gate so that visitors do not embarrass the residents. Guinness lists it as the largest collection in the world. The institution that banned the figure from its flower show in 1912 sits a hundred and eighty miles east. The ground has since been sold for housing and the collection has moved.
suggested_refs: The Gnome Reserve, West Putford, Devon
Guinness World Records, 'Largest collection of gnomes and pixies'

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Willi leaves the firm that bears his name
stops.date_confidence: attested.
stops.campa: Willi Griebel leaves the company. It has been the state's for eight years and his family's for a hundred and six, and he has been managing, under another sign, the works his grandfather built. He will live another twenty years and see it handed back to his son. For a decade there is no Griebel in the Gartenzwergmanufaktur Philipp Griebel, and the name on the letterhead belongs to a man of whom nobody now knows the birth year, the birthplace, or the resting place. The firm is by this point older than the state that owns it and will outlast it by a wide margin.
suggested_refs: Willi Griebel's departure from the nationalized works, 1980

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Reinhard reopens
stops.date_confidence: attested. The firm's registered name is Gartenzwergmanufaktur Philipp Griebel; the pool twice styled it 'Zwergenmanufaktur', which is wrong.
stops.campa: In the year of reunification Reinhard Griebel takes the firm back into private hands and opens the Zwergenstübchen, the little gnome parlour. Hand-thrown, hand-painted, one mould at a time, into a market now flooded with plastic gnomes cast by the thousand. The trading name is still Gartenzwergmanufaktur Philipp Griebel. Its founder has been dead for ninety-seven years, has no recorded birthday, and is nevertheless the name over the door of a functioning German company.
suggested_refs: Zwergenstübchen, Gräfenroda, opened 1990

stops.name: Gräfenroda, the museum
stops.date_confidence: decade only: the source says 'late 1990s'. The pool's 1998 came from a search summary and is invented precision.
stops.campa: Reinhard Griebel opens a garden gnome museum beside the works, and the object acquires the full apparatus of heritage: vitrines, labels, a chronology, a claim of primacy. What the museum cannot exhibit is its founder's founder. There is no portrait of Philipp Griebel, no signature, no tool identified as his, no grave to point visitors toward. A museum of the gnome stands on the ground where the biography of its maker should be, and the exhibit that would settle every contradiction in his biography, one certificate from Heinrich Dornheim, is described on the firm's website and shown to nobody.
suggested_refs: Garden Gnome Museum, Gräfenroda

stops.name: Briey, eleven from a bridge
stops.date_confidence: attested; widely reported, though the primary press record was not consulted directly.
stops.campa: The people of Briey wake to find eleven garden gnomes hanging by nooses from a road bridge, with a note. The Front de Libération des Nains de Jardin calls it a mass suicide and explains that the gnomes preferred death to a life spent as decoration. The joke is French and the target is Thuringian: a working man modelled from working men, sold as kitsch across a century, and now hanged in effigy for having consented to it. The group has been operating since the mid-1990s and will keep at it for years, stealing gnomes from suburban lawns and releasing them into woodland, and it is the only political movement the object has ever produced.
suggested_refs: Front de Libération des Nains de Jardin, Briey action, 1998

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Willi Griebel dies
stops.date_confidence: attested by the manufactory's own history page only.
stops.campa: Willi Griebel dies at eighty, the last of the family to have run the works before the state took them and the only one to have run them under three German regimes. His son has had the firm back for ten years. Of the four generations, only the first is undocumented, and he is the one whose name is on the door and on every box that leaves the yard. Willi's own dates rest on a single web page maintained by the company he worked for, which is more evidence than exists for his grandfather and less than exists for any of the gnomes.
suggested_refs: Willi Griebel, 1920-2000

stops.name: Paris, twenty liberated overnight
stops.date_confidence: attested for the theft. The pool's identification of the venue as Porte de Versailles and its figure of 2,000 gnomes on display appear in no source and are dropped; the canonical Paris pin is used instead.
stops.campa: The Front de Libération des Nains de Jardin takes twenty gnomes out of a Paris garden exhibition in the course of one night and issues its standing demand: that gnomes be returned to their natural habitat, the forest, rather than displayed for the amusement of gardeners. Members will be prosecuted and fined, the campaign will run for years, and imitators will appear in Italy and Germany, each raid framed as liberation rather than theft. Paris has hosted odder crimes than this, but never before a burglary of clay men.
suggested_refs: Front de Libération des Nains de Jardin, Paris exhibition raid, 2000

stops.name: Montmartre, the gnome that travels
stops.date_confidence: attested for the film and its effect.
stops.campa: Amélie Poulain steals her father's garden gnome and gives it to an air hostess, who photographs it before Red Square, the Angkor temples and the Manhattan skyline and posts the pictures home until the old man packs a suitcase himself. The film makes a worldwide practice of a prank that already existed, and for the second time in the object's history a piece of popular cinema does more for its distribution than any trade fair. Gräfenroda has no part in it and makes no claim on it.
suggested_refs: Le Fabuleux Destin d'Amélie Poulain, 2001
Café des Deux Moulins, Montmartre

stops.name: Southlake, the Roaming Gnome
stops.date_confidence: reported [R]: press accounts (Slate, Christian Science Monitor); the campaign budget and the three-month teaser interval are not independently verified.
stops.campa: Travelocity, out of its offices in Southlake, Texas, spends eighty-eight million dollars on an advertising campaign built around a garden gnome with a British accent, three months after teasing the public with a gnome reported missing. He is called the Roaming Gnome and he will be photographed at every landmark a travel budget can reach, from the Golden Gate Bridge outward. A hundred and twenty-nine years after a Thuringian modeller opened a shed, his product is an American corporate mascot with a passport.
suggested_refs: Travelocity Roaming Gnome campaign, from December 2003
sources: Christian Science Monitor, 'Roaming gnomes in the news again'

stops.name: Ames, fifteen feet of concrete
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the pool said the installation date could not be found, and it can. Timed to the fortieth anniversary of Earth Day.
stops.campa: Elwood is unveiled at Reiman Gardens on the fortieth anniversary of Earth Day: fifteen feet, three thousand five hundred pounds, poured in concrete by Andy and Connie Kautza of Wausau, Wisconsin, and certified by Guinness as the largest concrete garden gnome in the world. He displaces a previous holder at Kerhonkson, New York. Taller gnomes exist in fiberglass in Poland and in Canada, which is why the record has to name its material. The Gräfenroda originals stand about a foot high.

stops.name: Royal Hospital Chelsea, the ban lifted
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the celebrities; the day is show week rather than a sourced date.
stops.campa: For its centenary the Chelsea Flower Show suspends the hundred-year ban and lets the gnomes in for a single season. Elton John, Judi Dench and Dolly Parton are among the celebrities handed a blank gnome to paint; the results go to auction on eBay for the RHS Centenary Appeal and the Campaign for School Gardening, and Elton John's fetches over two thousand pounds. The ban is reinstated afterward and lifted again in 2026. The figure is readmitted as a joke about itself.

sources: NBC News, 'Banned garden gnomes make triumphant return to Chelsea Flower Show'

stops.name: Gräfenroda, Zwergstatt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month (January 2021, de.wikipedia). The 'last traditional manufactory' claim attached to it is the firm's own and is unverified.
stops.campa: Reinhard Griebel retires, and Helma Ortmann and Heidrun Viehweg take over the firm and the museum, trading from January 2021 as Zwergstatt Gräfenroda. For the first time since 1874 the works is not run by a Griebel. The house describes itself as the last traditional ceramic garden gnome manufactory in the world, and elsewhere as the last in Germany; the two scopes come out of the same marketing copy and neither is independently verified. It is recorded here as a claim the house makes about itself.
stops.quote: Seit Januar 2021 wird das Traditionsunternehmen und das Museum von Helma Ortmann und Heidrun Viehweg unter dem Namen 'Zwergstatt Gräfenroda' weitergeführt.

stops.name: Gräfenroda, entered on the register
stops.date_confidence: unverified. The listing turns up in German-language results, but no source gives a month or a year; the pool's 'March 2022' could not be confirmed, the cited page does not mention the inscription at all on fetch, and das-ist-thueringen.de returns 404.
stops.campa: The Gräfenroda garden gnomes are entered on Thuringia's register of Intangible Cultural Heritage. The craft is protected; the craftsman is not recovered. There is still no birth year, no birthplace, no grave and not one sentence anybody heard Philipp Griebel say. What the register holds is a village, a clay, a red cap and a collective form that his own descendants have always described as the work of several hands, one of which was his. Not even the date of the inscription can be established: the listing exists, and the year attached to it in the research pool is in no source that answers.
